title: Enterprise buyers criteria matrix and procurement playbook for model sourcing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a practical, sales-facing procurement playbook and an enterprise buyers criteria matrix for model sourcing decisions. Aim: reduce deal friction and RFP cycles by equipping Sales, Solutions Engineering, and Legal with a single artifact that maps buyer priorities (latency, cost, data residency, SLA, fallback strategy, explainability, quantization support) to recommended Redwood offerings (hosted, dedicated, private) and negotiation guardrails.
deliverables: 1) Buyers criteria matrix (spreadsheet + one-pager) mapping 12 enterprise concerns to negotiation language and product config recommendations; 2) Procurement playbook (confluence + slide deck) with clause templates for SLAs, substitution fallback, data residency, and audit rights; 3) Sales enablement notes and an FAQ; 4) Hand-off checklist for Legal/Account teams.
acceptance_criteria: - Matrix vetted by Sales (>=3 AE/SE interviews) and Legal; - Engineering verifies feasibility of recommended configs for Dedicated and Private; - At least two pilot deals use the playbook during negotiation; - Playbook published in Confluence and linked from Sales playbooks.

notes: Research highlights: customers equate 'substitution' with a contractual right to a model of equal or better latency+cost profile; many legal teams will not accept a broad 'compatibility' clause without quant metrics. Action: add measurable substitution triggers (p99, token cost, model island availability). Also recommend a quick-reference 'deployment choice guide' mapping business need -> hosted/dedicated/private with estimated procurement timelines. Consider packaging a RapidPrivate option (pre-approved hardware profile + SOW) to shorten time-to-deploy for high-value deals.
